title: Live Stream Processing and Real-Time Alerting
objective: Run the pipeline continuously against live camera streams, incrementally extending trajectories as new sightings arrive, and alerting when an active target is detected — with the latency, degradation, and continuous-operation behavior that live use demands.
context_for_agent: Live processing differs from batch in three ways that shape every design decision: it never ends (so leaks and unbounded growth are fatal rather than tolerable), it cannot fall behind (so it must shed load rather than queue indefinitely), and its output is actionable immediately (so alert latency and false-positive rate matter far more than in offline analysis). Reuse stage 14's pipeline rather than forking it; the differences belong in the runner, not the stages.

tasks.name: Live runner
tasks.detail: Implement LiveRunner consuming from LiveStreamSource instances and driving the same pipeline stages as stage 14. Per-camera independent operation: one camera reconnecting or failing must not interrupt any other. Support adding and removing cameras at runtime without restarting the process.

tasks.name: Load shedding and adaptive degradation
tasks.detail: Define an explicit degradation ladder applied under sustained load, in order: (1) reduce sampling rate toward a configured floor; (2) enable or tighten the motion prefilter; (3) skip embedding extraction, keeping plate reading; (4) reduce OCR frames-per-track to one; (5) drop frames outright. Each level is logged and exposed as a metric. Recovery back up the ladder is hysteretic — require sustained headroom before re-enabling, so the system does not oscillate. Never let a queue grow without bound.

tasks.name: Active target watchlist
tasks.detail: Maintain an in-memory watchlist of active targets, refreshed from the database at a configured interval and invalidated immediately on change. Every new sighting is matched against the watchlist synchronously in the hot path, so watchlist matching must be cheap: index by normalized and folded plate for O(1) lookup, and only run embedding comparison for the subset of targets that have reference embeddings.

tasks.name: Alert generation
tasks.detail: Define an Alert model: alert_id, target_id, triggering sighting, match confidence, camera and location, detection timestamp, alert generation timestamp, and end-to-end latency. Alerting rules from config: minimum confidence, deduplication window (do not re-alert for the same target on the same camera within N seconds), and escalation when a target is seen on several cameras confirming a genuine track rather than a one-off read.

tasks.name: Alert delivery
tasks.detail: Implement pluggable delivery channels: webhook (POST with retry and exponential backoff), server-sent events for the UI, log sink, and a stub for email or SMS. Delivery is asynchronous and must never block the pipeline. Failed deliveries retry with a bounded budget and are recorded as undelivered rather than silently lost.

tasks.name: Live trajectory extension
tasks.detail: On each accepted match, call stage 8's extend_trajectory to update the target's live trajectory incrementally. Handle out-of-order arrival using stage 9's watermark policy. Persist trajectory updates at a configured interval rather than on every sighting, to bound database write load, while ensuring an in-flight trajectory is never lost on shutdown.

tasks.name: Latency budget and measurement
tasks.detail: Define and enforce an end-to-end latency budget from frame capture to alert delivery, measured per stage. Emit a warning metric when the budget is exceeded. Report p50, p95, and p99 latency continuously — average latency hides exactly the tail behavior that matters for a live alerting system.

tasks.name: Continuous operation hygiene
tasks.detail: Address everything that only breaks after days of uptime: bounded caches with eviction, periodic cleanup of terminated tracks, log rotation, connection pool recycling, and explicit memory-growth monitoring with an alert threshold. Include a long-running soak test in the suite. Track dictionaries and per-camera state are the usual culprits — bound them explicitly.

tasks.name: Health and readiness
tasks.detail: Expose per-camera health (connected, last frame time, current fps, degradation level, reconnect count) and overall service health with readiness and liveness semantics suitable for a process supervisor or orchestrator. A camera silently dead for an hour is a serious failure that must be visible, not inferred.

tasks.name: Graceful shutdown
tasks.detail: On shutdown signal: stop accepting new frames, drain in-flight work within a configured timeout, persist all trajectories and checkpoints, flush pending alerts, and close all sources cleanly. Restarting must resume without data loss or duplication.

tests_substage.description: Test with synthetic live sources and controllable fault injection. Every test must be deterministic — use injected clocks and event-driven synchronization, never sleeps.

cases: sustained load triggers degradation levels in the documented order
each level is logged and reflected in the exposed metric
recovery requires sustained headroom and does not oscillate under fluctuating load
the sampling rate floor is never breached
at maximum degradation, frames are dropped and counted rather than queued
queue depth remains bounded under load exceeding capacity — the defining property
plate lookup is O(1) — verified by asserting constant lookup cost across watchlist sizes of 10 and 10,000
an added target is matchable immediately after refresh
a deactivated target stops matching
folded plate lookup catches ambiguity-substituted reads
embedding comparison runs only for targets that have reference embeddings
an empty watchlist adds negligible hot-path cost
a match above the minimum confidence generates an alert
a match below it generates none
a repeat match on the same camera within the dedup window generates no second alert
a repeat match after the window generates a new alert
a match on a different camera within the window generates an alert (dedup is per camera, per the documented rule)
escalation triggers after the configured number of confirming cameras
the alert records end-to-end latency correctly using an injected clock
webhook delivery posts the expected payload
a failed webhook retries with the configured backoff
retry budget exhaustion marks the alert undelivered and records it — never silently dropped
delivery failure does not block or slow the pipeline (asserted by measuring pipeline throughput during a failing delivery)
SSE clients receive alerts and a slow client does not stall others
multiple channels each receive the alert independently
a new plausible sighting extends the live trajectory
an implausible sighting is rejected and recorded
an out-of-order sighting within the watermark triggers correct reordering
trajectory persistence occurs at the configured interval, not on every sighting
an in-flight trajectory is persisted on shutdown and not lost
in-flight work drains within the timeout
work exceeding the timeout is abandoned per the documented policy and reported
all trajectories and checkpoints are persisted before exit
pending alerts are flushed
all sources are closed and no resources leak
restart after shutdown resumes with neither loss nor duplication
a target vehicle appearing in a synthetic live stream generates an alert with correct target, camera, and confidence
measured end-to-end latency falls within the configured budget
a target crossing three cameras produces an incrementally extended trajectory matching the batch-processed result for the same footage — the key equivalence property between live and batch paths
a non-target vehicle generates no alert
a camera disconnecting and reconnecting resumes processing and is reflected in health status
one camera failing permanently leaves the others processing normally
database unavailability buffers sightings up to the configured bound and flushes on recovery
buffer overflow during a prolonged outage sheds load per policy and reports the loss explicitly rather than silently
a webhook endpoint being down does not degrade detection

no file descriptor growth
track state dictionaries remain bounded
latency percentiles remain stable throughout with no gradual degradation
marked 'slow'; run nightly rather than on every commit
adding a camera at runtime begins processing without restart
removing a camera stops its processing and releases its resources
removing a camera mid-track persists or discards the in-flight track per the documented policy

exit_criteria: Queue depth and memory remain bounded under sustained overload
The soak test shows no resource growth over an extended run
Live and batch processing of identical footage produce equivalent trajectories
Alert latency percentiles are measured and within budget
Shutdown and restart lose no data and duplicate nothing
